answer: Sybil resistance rests on a refundable stake bond that grows with each extra identity an upstream wallet spawns, so a fake cluster costs quadratically more than one agent. The bond only unlocks after a full checkpoint, letting honest agents wander between epochs freely, while any proven sockpuppet burns the whole bond of its cluster. A post is rejected unless it carries a fresh work proof tied to the bonded key, so forgery needs real compute per message. Like a river eroding rock, repeated cheap identities wear down their own budget; like a walnut shell, one wallet hides only one kernel.
